groups.definition: L5-01 and L5-02 contrast a habitual morning action with its negated form. Preserve the habitual time, subject and object. Both sentences describe a habit.
L5-03 and L5-04 use the same motion frame and school destination. L5-03 says the past trip occurred. L5-04 negates that trip. The rows share a frame, not a completed event.
L4-01 and L4-02 share ongoing rain as the reason for studying at home. L4-02 adds an explicit intention. The two sentences share the cause and differ in intention. Both leave the actor unnamed.
L4-03 and L4-04 contrast walking to a station with walking from it, followed by meeting a friend. They do not state where the meeting occurs or prove that it happens during the walk.

L3-01 says the train delay caused the person to miss the meeting start time. L3-02 treats the delay as a concession and says the person arrived before the meeting started. Both leave the arriving person unstated. Relation and outcome differ, so this pair does not isolate the connective.
L3-03 and L3-04 contrast coughs gradually improving with a completed recovery after taking medicine. Neither states who took the medicine.
L2-01 and L2-02 contrast a condition that avoids spending meeting time on detail checks with a concession where checks remain necessary. The relation and result both differ.

L2-03 and L2-04 contrast an established arrangement to notify people after confirmation with the speaker's intention to notify them. The Japanese does not identify the notifier in L2-03 or the speaker in L2-04.
L1-01 rejects the inference that a delayed review means lower workload. L1-02 says the delay leaves a lower workload uncertain. Both leave the actual workload open.

L1-03 contrasts an appearance of acknowledging facts with omission of the key decision process. L1-04 states that facts are acknowledged and the process is also addressed. This is not a simple positive/negative pair.

HS-01 and HS-02 use the same name and place. They change が to は and switch from present to absent. HS-03 and HS-04 use the hiragana name さくら. They change last week to next week and past to nonpast. HS-05 and HS-06 use katakana アレックス. They also change が to は, affirmative to not-yet negative, and add その and まだ. These pairs vary several features, so they are not single-feature controls. HS-12 uses the name honorific 佐藤さん and includes a teacher-title clause. HS-11 belongs to non_name_san_boundaries and uses さんま as a fish name. These are cross-group contexts, not an in-group matched pair. Do not infer gender or a unique spelling from さん.
HS-07 states that the person is male. HS-08 states the teacher role and leaves gender unspecified. These cases use different contexts.

HS-09 preserves the kinship meaning in お母さん. HS-10 preserves the clerk role in 店員さん. HS-11 treats さんま as a fish name, not a name suffix. These rows cover distinct lexical and role boundaries. HS-12 is in personal_name_honorific_gender_neutrality and uses 佐藤さん as a name honorific. HS-11 and HS-12 are cross-group contexts, not a matched pair.
